name: py-spy, scalene, and stay-vs-Rust performance gate
short_definition: How to measure Python service performance before optimizing or rewriting: py-spy for low-overhead production sampling (attach to PID, flame graphs); scalene for high-resolution CPU/GPU/memory profiling in staging/dev; cProfile/pyinstrument for simple call graphs; memray for allocation-heavy leaks. The stay-vs-Rust gate is evidence-based — only hand off to Axum/Rust after profiles show CPU-bound Python that resists algorithmic and I/O fixes, not because microbenchmarks or resume-driven rewrite. As of 2026-07-13: py-spy 0.4.2, scalene 2.3.0, memray 1.19.3.
scope_in: Profiler selection matrix; production-safe sampling; staging deep profiles; interpreting flame graphs vs line profiles; distinguishing DB/network wait from Python CPU; memory leak tools; load-test + profile loop; criteria to stay in Python vs extract Rust; agent rules against premature rewrite; linking to observability (OTel latency).
scope_out: Language decision catalog in full (py-vs-ts-vs-rust); ASGI server swap vanity benches (py-asgi-servers); msgspec vs Pydantic micro-opts (py-msgspec-hotpath); full Rust Axum design (rust.md); free-threading production claims.
defaults: Production incident or p99 spike: attach py-spy (record/top/dump) for 30–120s during load — no code change, low overhead, safe enough for careful prod use. Local/staging optimization: scalene for CPU+memory line-level (and GPU if used); optional pyinstrument for readable call trees; cProfile+snakeviz for stdlib-only environments. Memory growth: memray. Always pair profile with metrics (OTel, /metrics) and a reproducible load (k6/locust/vegeta). Optimization order: measure → fix queries/N+1/pools/timeouts → algorithmic/data structure → batching/cache → native/Rust extract. Do not switch languages on hello-world RPS.
decision_gates: USE py-spy when process is running (prod/staging) and you need CPU stacks now. USE scalene when you can restart under profiler and need Python-vs-native and memory attribution. USE memray for RSS climb / allocation hotspots. STAY in Python when profile is wait-dominated (DB, HTTP, Redis, LLM APIs) or when caching/query fix yields enough. MOVE to Rust (or Cython/native only with strong reason) when: measured CPU-bound pure-Python hot loop after algorithm fix; latency SLA requires sub-ms/microbatch throughput Python cannot hit; isolation of untrusted/CPU-heavy workload. DO NOT rewrite for aesthetic preference. DO NOT use cProfile alone in multi-threaded/async production as truth without sampling confirmation.
do_dont: DO: capture baseline p50/p99 first; profile under realistic load; label profiles with git sha; fix I/O before CPU; document stay-vs-Rust decision with flame graph evidence; keep py-spy in ops toolbox (sidecar or ephemeral debug). DON'T: optimize without profile; trust microbench of JSON alone; rewrite whole service to Rust for one endpoint without extract option; leave continuous high-overhead profilers on prod 24/7; ship debug symbols secrets; confuse GIL wait with useful work without care.
code_skeleton:
# --- py-spy (production attach; needs ptrace/sys_ptrace or --pid permissions) ---
# uv tool install py-spy  # or system package
# py-spy top --pid $PID
# py-spy record -o profile.svg --pid $PID --duration 60
# py-spy record -o profile.svg --subprocesses -- python -m mypkg

# --- scalene (dev/staging) ---
# uv add --dev scalene
# uv run scalene --cpu --memory --html mypkg/benchmark_entry.py
# uv run scalene --outfile profile.html -- mypkg/cli.py serve

# --- cProfile quick ---
# uv run python -m cProfile -o out.prof -m mypkg.worker
# uv run snakeviz out.prof

# --- memray ---
# uv add --dev memray
# uv run memray run -o out.bin python -m mypkg
# uv run memray flamegraph out.bin

# --- stay-vs-Rust gate checklist (record in ADR) ---
# 1) OTel shows endpoint X p99 = T
# 2) py-spy: % time in module Y (CPU) vs greenlet/await wait
# 3) Optimized query/cache/algorithm → still fail SLA?
# 4) Extract boundary: OpenAPI endpoint or queue consumer → Rust
# 5) One owner for data path; contract tests
failure_modes: 1) Optimizing the wrong 5% visible in microbench. 2) Treating DB wait as Python CPU. 3) py-spy denied (no ptrace) → empty conclusions. 4) Profiler overhead skews timings (heavy instrumentation in prod). 5) Async stack collapsed poorly → misread. 6) Premature Rust rewrite doubles ops surface without SLA win. 7) Memory leak misdiagnosed as traffic growth. 8) No load generator → profile of idle process. 9) Free-threaded Python assumptions without verification.
anti_patterns: Agents must not: recommend Rust rewrite without profile evidence; default to Cython for all hot paths; use time.sleep benchmarks as capacity planning; leave scalene on prod web workers permanently; claim Uvicorn→Granian replaces algorithm work; paste synthetic RPS as architecture ADR alone.
tools: Primary: py-spy (prod sampling), scalene (dev CPU/mem/GPU), memray (allocations), cProfile/pyinstrument (dev call graphs), OTel metrics/traces (always-on). Load: k6, locust, vegeta. Optional: yappi, Austin, perf+flamegraph for native. Not default: custom print-timing spaghetti as only method.
versions_as_of: as_of 2026-07-13 — py-spy 0.4.2 (PyPI); scalene 2.3.0; memray 1.19.3; yappi 1.7.6; line_profiler 5.0.2. Install profilers as dev/ops tools — not runtime service dependencies unless deliberate.

deprecation_watch: Resume-driven full rewrites; continuous cProfile in prod; ignoring async I/O wait; free-threaded magic as free speedup without measure; only optimizing JSON library when DB is 90% of time.
ts_boundary: Next/TS profiling is different (React/Chrome perf, Node clinic). For BFF→Python latency, measure both sides (fetch timeout, TTFB). Do not rewrite Python service because Next LCP is bad — separate concerns. Shared: OpenAPI latency SLOs.
rust_boundary: This item is the gate into rust.md 'When to use Rust'. After evidence, extract hot path as Axum service or worker; keep Python for AI/orchestration. Contract-first OpenAPI/proto; one table owner. Don't dual-write during migration without ADR.
supabase_boundary: Most 'Python is slow' SaaS profiles are Postgres/RLS/query plans. EXPLAIN ANALYZE and pool sizing (py-db-pool-lifecycle) before language change. Service role vs user JWT changes plans — profile the real auth path.
boundary_contracts: SLO document (p99 targets); ADR for language extract; OpenAPI for extracted endpoints; profile artifacts retained with release notes when deciding rewrite; env flags for optional debug (never leave on).
decision_matrix_row: Problem: unknown latency → py-spy + OTel first. Problem: CPU+memory line detail → scalene. Problem: RSS leak → memray. Problem: wait-bound I/O → stay Python, fix pools/queries. Problem: measured CPU-bound pure Python failing SLA after optimize → Rust extract. Problem: UI jank → TS/frontend tools not Python rewrite.
threats: Granting SYS_PTRACE broadly increases escape risk; profile files may contain PII/query params; debug endpoints exposing profilers publicly; resource exhaustion via always-on heavy profilers.
mitigations: Time-boxed attach; least privilege debug; scrub profile args; no public /debug/pprof without auth; prefer sampling over instrumenting every request in prod; store profiles in private bucket.
agent_codegen_policy: MUST: recommend measure-before-optimize; name py-spy for live, scalene for deep; check I/O/DB first; require evidence before Rust. MUST NOT: rewrite service to Rust as first response to 'slow'; invent Cython by default; enable permanent high-overhead profiling in prod templates.
tests_required: Optional performance regression tests only for critical hot paths with stable fixtures (careful flakiness). Unit tests for algorithmic fixes. Contract tests after Rust extract. Load test script versioned for replay.
ci_gates: Not a blocking PR gate by default. Optional nightly bench. Require ADR link for language extract PRs. Ban agents auto-adding always-on profilers to prod Docker CMD.
skill_scan_signals: POSITIVE: py-spy/scalene docs in runbooks; OTel latency; ADR for Rust extract; load test scripts. NEGATIVE: rewrite-to-Rust without metrics; cProfile-only production claims; optimize without baseline; hello-world RPS architecture decisions.
skill_module_bullets: Profile before optimize: py-spy (prod sample), scalene (CPU/mem dev), memray (allocations).
Most SaaS slowness is DB/network/LLM wait — fix pools and queries first.
Stay-vs-Rust gate: measured CPU-bound Python failing SLA after algorithm/I/O fixes → extract Axum service.
Do not rewrite languages for vanity RPS or without flame graph evidence.
Pair profilers with OTel p99 and reproducible load generators.
Never leave high-overhead profilers on permanent prod web paths.
action_items: Add stay-vs-Rust checklist to references/python.md and link rust.md.
Runbook: py-spy attach steps per host (Fly/K8s).
Scan agent prompts for premature Rust rewrite.
Optional nightly bench job for critical workers only.
checklist: Only then consider Rust extract + ADR
Contract + one table owner for extract
No permanent heavy profiler in prod CMD
conflicts_noted: py-spy needs elevated/ptrace rights — some PaaS block attach entirely (use staging twin). Scalene AI suggestions are optional UX not source of truth. Community debates continuous profiling products (Pyroscope etc.) vs ad-hoc py-spy — either fine; always-on commercial continuous profiling out of default greenfield scope. GIL vs free-threading: do not assume free-threading solves multi-core without re-measure.
